level.label: A₁ crosses into its memory lane

events.text: Routing begins (ticks 0–15). The train of K = 12 slots (A₁ at the front, D̃₂↓ at the tail) enters the input port one site per tick. Every walker sits on one of two trees, ↑ (bit 0) or ↓ (bit 1), and every carrier has a backup on each tree. Each tree runs the backup protocol: Û_in copies the colour of A_d onto its backup on the same tree, Û_B (blue control) passes the bit two walkers at a time. At each bifurcation Ŝ⁽↓⁾ = Ŝ sends red walkers left and blue ones right, Ŝ⁽↑⁾ = Ŝ X̂ the opposite, resetting the colour to red: the two trees are photographic negatives of each other.
A₁ enters the tree at the input port (edge (1,1), site 1).
Ã₁↑ enters the tree at the input port (edge (1,1), site 1).
Ã₁↓ enters the tree at the input port (edge (1,1), site 1).

Ã₂↓ enters the tree at the input port (edge (1,1), site 1).

Û_B⁽¹⁾ [Ã₁↑, Ã₁↓] on edge (1,1): Ã₁↓ is blue → X̂ flips Ã₂↓.
Ŝ: Ã₁↑ ↑R at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ: Ã₁↓ ↓B at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), reset to red.

D̃₁↓ enters the tree at the input port (edge (1,1), site 1).

Ŝ: Ã₂↑ ↑R at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ: Ã₂↓ ↓B at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), reset to red.

Û_in⁽²⁾ on the 2 edges of level 2: A₂ is red → X̂ flips Ã₂↑.

Û_B⁽²⁾ [Ã₂↑, Ã₂↓] on the 2 edges of level 2: Ã₂↓ is blue → X̂ flips D̃₁↑.
Ŝ: Ã₂↑ ↑B at node (2,2) → left into (3,3), reset to red.
Ŝ: Ã₂↓ ↓R at node (2,2) → left into (3,3), stays red.
Ŝ: D̃₂↑ ↑R at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ: D̃₂↓ ↓B at node (1,1) → right into (2,2), reset to red.
Ŝ: D₁ ↓R at node (2,2) → left into (3,3), stays red.
Û_B⁽²⁾ [D̃₁↑, D̃₁↓] on the 2 edges of level 2: D̃₁↓ is blue → X̂ flips D̃₂↑.
Ŝ: D̃₁↑ ↑B at node (2,2) → left into (3,3), reset to red.

Ŝ: D₂ ↓R at node (2,2) → left into (3,3), stays red.

Query (ticks 16–20). Every walker rests in a memory lane (each slot on its own lane site). Each data walker D_j is copied under the control of the backup in front of it (Ã_n↓ for D₁, D̃_{j−1}↓ for D_j): the backups are present and red only in the lane(s) the train reached. The local copy Û_copy^loc(D_j|M_j) turns D_j blue where the stored bit b_j = 0. Then the output circuit of the cell moves the blue data walkers to the ↑ tree: Ŝ_M sends them to the auxiliary rail, Ŝ_M† onto ↑ (blue) and the clocked X̂_c resets them to red.
Û_copy [D₁ | Ã₂↓] acts in the lane(s) where Ã₂↓ is red: the local copy turns blue D₁ in 1 branch(es).
Û_copy [D₂ | D̃₁↓] acts in the lane(s) where D̃₁↓ is red: the local copy leaves the data walkers red (stored bits = 1).
Ŝ_M (output circuit of the cells) sends the blue data walkers of the ↓ lane to the auxiliary rail, red: D₁.
Ŝ_M† (output circuit of the cells) merges the auxiliary rail into the ↑ lane: the walkers arrive blue: D₁.
X̂_c (output circuit of the cells) resets the data walkers on the ↑ lane to red (clocked colour NOT): D₁.
End of the query: every walker reverses its direction; the inverse routing replays the forward schedule backwards in time.

Inverse routing (ticks 21–36): the exact time reversal of routing. The train retraces its path tail-first; Ŝ† merges the paths at every bifurcation (a red walker arriving from the right child turns blue) and the same gates fire again in reverse order, recollecting the dispersed address walkers. All 2 levels are undone and the walkers leave through the port they entered.

Ŝ†: D̃₁↓ arrives ↓R from the left child (3,3) → up into (2,2), stays red.
Û_B⁽²⁾ [D̃₁↑, D̃₁↓] (inverse routing; self-adjoint) on the 2 edges of level 2: D̃₁↓ is blue → X̂ flips D̃₂↑.
Ŝ†: D₁ arrives ↑R from the left child (3,3) → up into (2,2), turns blue.
Ŝ†: Ã₂↑ arrives ↑R from the left child (3,3) → up into (2,2), turns blue.

Ŝ†: D̃₂↑ arrives ↑R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), stays red.
Ŝ†: D̃₂↓ arrives ↓R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), turns blue.
Û_B⁽²⁾ [Ã₂↑, Ã₂↓] (inverse routing; self-adjoint) on the 2 edges of level 2: Ã₂↓ is blue → X̂ flips D₁, D̃₁↑.
Ŝ†: A₂ arrives ↑R from the right child (3,4) → up into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ†: D₂ arrives ↓R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), turns blue.
Ŝ†: Ã₁↑ arrives ↑R from the right child (3,4) → up into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ†: Ã₁↓ arrives ↓R from the left child (3,3) → up into (2,2), stays red.
Ŝ†: D̃₁↑ arrives ↑R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), stays red.
Ŝ†: D̃₁↓ arrives ↓R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), turns blue.
Û_B⁽¹⁾ [D̃₁↑, D̃₁↓] (inverse routing; self-adjoint) on edge (1,1): D̃₁↓ is blue → X̂ flips D₂, D̃₂↓.
Û_in⁽²⁾ (inverse routing; self-adjoint) on the 2 edges of level 2: A₂ is red → X̂ flips Ã₂↑.
Ŝ†: A₁ arrives ↓R from the left child (3,1) → up into (2,1), stays red.
Ŝ†: D₁ arrives ↑R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), stays red.
Ŝ†: Ã₂↑ arrives ↑R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), stays red.
Ŝ†: Ã₂↓ arrives ↓R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), turns blue.
D̃₂↑ leaves the tree through the port.
D̃₂↓ leaves the tree through the port.

Ŝ†: A₂ arrives ↑R from the right child (2,2) → up into (1,1), stays red.
D₂ leaves the tree through the port.

paper.source: the technical paper, §Backup variant for dual-rail implementation, Resource scalings
paper.engine_depth_formula: 2(4n + 2(n + m)) + T_q (memory lane hosting the train)

notes: Two trees: sites_total counts both; sites_path is one root-to-cell path. The walkers start on their rails: the paper's T_prep is not simulated.
The output circuit of the cells (Ŝ_M, Ŝ_M†, X̂_c) runs in the lane during the query (three ticks after the copies).
The memory lane hosts the whole train at rest: T_total = 2·T_fwd + T_q, not the paper's pass-through depth constant.
